title: Rajasthan District Gazetteers: Bikaner (K.K. Sehgal, 1972) - lifeways sections re-read
what_it_contains: Food p.114 (leaf 133): staple bajra; moth main pulse; 'Gawar-ki-phali' eaten with thick bajra bread 'Sogra'; kachri, sangri (khejri pod, leaves eaten in famines), tindsi/phofalia, kair and phog pods as condiments; watermelon and ber; 'Kichra' speciality of Akha Teej; Bikaner rasgulla, papad, bhujia. Dwellings p.111 (leaf 130): circular mud/thatch huts (OCR 'jitopcia' = jhompa), separate grain store 'Kotlia', kitchen, cattle-shed that doubles as guest room, 'paidwa' gable huts, thorn hedges against sand drift. Language p.89 (1961): Marwari 372,833; Rathi 2,156; Thali 475. Music p.120: songs to 'Chang' (sheep-skin drum), Holi 'rammat'; games p.120: kabaddi, 'Mar pari', gulli-danda, lathi, aankh-michoni, khoh; indoor chaupar, cards; swings in rains; kathputli p.122. Livestock p.137-139: Rathi and Sahiwal cows, Nagauri bullocks (draw water from deep wells), Pugal cows famed for milk; Bikaneri camel 1500 lb, 8.5 ft, camel hair strings, camel skin jars for ghee/oil; Camel Development Scheme 1959, breeding farm at Jorbir; Marwari goats; Magra sheep 3-5 lb wool/yr, Chokla, Nali; Appendix V p.154-155: Mahajan Cattle Fair 27.9-2.10.1958 (Rathi: 1,300 brought, 563 sold) and 19-25.2.1959 (Rathi: 1,275/138). Crafts p.156-171: blankets, lois (Napasar), 25,000 spinning/weaving families, 15,000 leather families, camel-hide 'kuppis' with gold lacquer (usta), Gangaur wooden toys made by 'one or two families', red-clay pottery, papad of moong+moth kneaded in sajji water. Fairs p.116-119 list Kenyara fair (Lunkaransar, Ramdev, Magh Sudi 10) but NOT Nathu Dada. Famine 1963-64: water by rail tanks and camels, 20,000 livestock moved to Suratgarh.
why_relevant: Best single printed baseline ('then') for almost every element in this track; page-level citations for the website.
found_via: history track file; grep in OCR

title: Powlett, Gazetteer of the Bikanir State (1874) - water, famine foods, phog
what_it_contains: p.82-84 (PDF p.105-107): wells 300+ ft deep near the city; villages sit in depressions on kankar so rain is caught 'in covered pits, called kunds'; '-sar' in village names means tank/depression; khejri pod 'sangri' plus leaves and bark eaten by the poor in famine; phog twigs and roots line shallow wells and build huts, green phog feeds camels, buds eaten with buttermilk in Feb-March; exile's couplet to the phog bush; karil (ker), tumba seeds pounded to flour, khimp, kachri; bharut grass seed 'more eaten by the very poor than any other grain'; p.85 (PDF 116): Pugal cows famous for milk and ghi; p.? (PDF 150) villages of huts, 'dhulkot' sand forts supported by phog stems.
why_relevant: Oldest local-language food/water vocabulary with page numbers: kund, sangri, phog, kachri, tumba.
found_via: history track file (history.jsonl); tesseract OCR re-read

title: Nanuram Sanskarta, 'Khed Rapat' (Kalu, Lunkaransar tehsil, 1984) - food, fodder, kund
what_it_contains: p.42 (leaf 74): local grasses (bhurat, sewan...), phog, khejri sangri, ker; kachri, phofaliya as vegetables; 'rabdi' made of chhach with bajra or jowar flour, proverb on rabdi; the Kalu milk cooperative now buys all the milk so 'chhach, dahi and rabdi have become old dreams' (Bagri/Rajasthani prose). p.464 (leaf 498): every person building a house made a small or big kund to catch roof water, used lota by lota; p.450: village Sui has more kunds because well water is not sweet; p.106: matira of the area.
why_relevant: A 1984 voice from Lunkaransar tehsil itself that already records a 'then and now' shift (milk sold to dairy, rabdi disappearing) - ideal quote for the site.
found_via: history track file; Hindi keyword grep

title: Anupam Mishra, 'Radiant Raindrops of Rajasthan' (English tr. of 'Rajasthan ki Rajat Boondein', 1995)
what_it_contains: PDF p.16-20: kuin (narrow deep well tapping 'rejani' moisture held above a gypsum layer; built by chelvanji/chejaro; lined with khimp rope coils; small charas used); 'a gypsum layer does run through Churu, Bikaner, Jaisalmer and Badmer: that is why, in these districts, kuins are to be found in each village' (p.20). p.20-22: kund/kundi with 'agor' catchment kept clean, domed covers, private and collective kundis, maintenance families. Also johar, nadi, beri, tanka, charas.
why_relevant: Authoritative, freely reusable description of every traditional water structure named in the brief; gives Bikaner-specific kuin claim.
